title: Plugin Manifest v1.1
description: The contract a plugin declares so the pipeline can load it without knowing its internals. v1.1 adds `role`/`consumes`, splits `irRange` into `acceptsIrRange` (emitter/sink) and `producesIrRange` (source), declares the hook->export load surface on `entrypoint`, lets an asset be a bundle directory carrying `sha256`/`bytes`/`brotliBytes`, and names the config's location. Version selection is explicit: a manifest that omits `manifestVersion` is a v1.0.0 manifest and keeps the v1.0.0 contract exactly (`irRange` only; `role`, `consumes`, `acceptsIrRange` and `producesIrRange` are rejected). Set `manifestVersion: "1.1.0"` to opt into the v1.1 rules. The additive fields (`entrypoint` object form, asset integrity/bundles, `config`) are accepted by both versions, so no v1.0.0 manifest needs to change.

manifestVersion.description: Which manifest contract this document is written against. Absent means `1.0.0` (the frozen original). `1.1.0` opts into the role, directional IR-range, hook-export, asset-integrity and config rules below.

role.description: Which seam this plugin sits on. Required in v1.1 and it decides which IR-range field is required and which artifact kinds `emits`/`consumes` must contain. A `source` reads the live site and produces Site IR; an `emitter` turns Site IR into a site artifact; a `sink` turns a form submission into a delivery and needs a server function (`api-functions`); a `deployer` pushes built artifacts to a host and speaks no IR.

irRange.description: v1.0.0 only: semver range of Site IR versions this plugin accepts or produces. Deprecated in v1.1, where the direction is explicit (`acceptsIrRange` or `producesIrRange`); a v1.1 manifest that keeps it is rejected rather than silently honoured.

acceptsIrRange.description: v1.1, required for `emitter` and `sink`: semver range of Site IR versions this plugin can read. Must accept `IR_VERSION` from `src/schema/site-ir.ts`.

producesIrRange.description: v1.1, required for `source`: semver range of Site IR versions this plugin emits. Must accept `IR_VERSION` from `src/schema/site-ir.ts`; a source that emits a version this repo cannot read is a conformance failure.

emits.description: Artifact kinds this plugin produces. v1.1 ties this to `role`: a source emits `site-ir`, an emitter emits `static-html` or `islands-wasm`, a sink emits `api-functions`, a deployer emits `deployment`.

consumes.description: v1.1: artifact kinds this plugin reads, which is what makes a source adapter distinguishable from an emitter. Required in v1.1: a source consumes nothing from the pipeline (empty array), an emitter consumes `site-ir`, a sink consumes `form-submission`, a deployer consumes at least one built artifact.

sinks.description: Submission targets this plugin handles. In v1.1 this is only meaningful for `role: "sink"`: a sink must declare at least one, and a plugin that declares one must be a sink.

hooks.description: Lifecycle hooks the pipeline will call, in `phase:name` form. Every hook listed here must be a callable function on the export named by `entrypoint.hooksExport`.

entrypoint.description: Where the loadable module is and which export holds the hook record. The v1.0.0 string form names only the module and assumes the `hooks` export; the object form declares both, which is what lets the conformance harness prove hook coverage. v1.1 requires the object form.

module.description: Plugin-relative path to the module the pipeline imports.

hooksExport.description: Named export on that module holding the hook record (`{ "capture:start": fn, ... }`).

assets.description: Files or bundle directories the plugin ships beside its code (templates, golden payloads, migration SQL, Wasm bundles). Paths are plugin-relative. A file asset may declare `sha256`/`bytes`/`brotliBytes`; a bundle declares `type: "directory"` and lists its members in `files[]`.

runbook.description: Path to this plugin's operator runbook, markdown.

configSchema.description: Plugin-relative path to the JSON Schema for this plugin's own configuration. v1.1 also requires `config` when this is present, so the loader can resolve the document the schema describes.

config.description: v1.1: where the plugin's configuration actually is, so a loader can resolve it instead of guessing from `configSchema`. Exactly one of `path` (a JSON document beside the plugin) or `inline` (the document, for a plugin with no file).

path.description: Plugin-relative path to the config document. JSON, because it is validated against `configSchema`.

inline.description: The config document itself, for a plugin whose config is not a shipped file.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the shipped bytes.

consumableKind.description: An artifact kind a plugin can read, plus `form-submission` for a sink: the visitor's POST, which is not a build artifact but is the sink's real input.

bundleFile.description: One member of a bundle directory. `path` is relative to the bundle's own directory, so a bundle can be moved without rewriting every member.

brotliBytes.description: Brotli-compressed size at quality 11 (what a CDN would serve). Required for a Wasm bundle member: the < 250 KB per-bundle budget is measured on this number.

wasmBundleFile.description: A bundle member that must also declare its compressed size, because the size budget is measured on brotli bytes.

optional.description: The asset may be absent on a fresh checkout. Nothing verifies integrity for an asset that is not there.

type.description: `file` (default) or `directory` for a bundle. A bundle carries its integrity per member, in `files[]`.

brotliBytes.description: Brotli-compressed size at quality 11. Declared for a Wasm file so the size budget is checkable from the manifest; the harness re-measures it and rejects a claim that does not match.

files.description: A bundle's members. Required when `type` is `directory`, forbidden otherwise.

allOf.description: `type: directory` is a bundle and must list its members; a file asset must not.
A Wasm asset must declare verifiable integrity: a file carries `sha256`/`bytes`/`brotliBytes`, a bundle carries them per member.

manifestV10.description: The frozen v1.0.0 contract: `irRange` is the only IR-version signal and the directional/role fields do not exist yet. This branch is what keeps every existing manifest valid.

manifestV11.description: The v1.1.0 contract: `role` decides which IR direction is required and which artifact kinds `emits`/`consumes` must contain, and the hook load surface is explicit.

allOf.description: A source reads the live site, produces Site IR, and reads nothing the pipeline built.
An emitter reads Site IR and produces a site artifact.
A sink turns a form submission into a delivery. It needs a server function, and it is the only role that may declare `sinks`.
A deployer pushes built artifacts to a host. It speaks no Site IR, so neither IR range applies.
`sinks` is not a comment: declaring a submission target makes the plugin a sink, and a sink must declare one.
